title: Jesus and the ‘prostitute.’ part 3
scripture_text: ‘’When one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to have dinner with him, he went to the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table. A woman in that town who lived a sinful life learned that Jesus was eating at the Pharisee’s house, so she came there with an alabaster jar of perfume. As she stood behind him at his feet weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears. Then she wiped them with her hair, kissed them and poured perfume on them. When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would know who is touching him and what kind of woman she is—that she is a sinner.” Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.” “Tell me, teacher,” he said. “Two people owed money to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. Neither of them had the money to pay him back, so he forgave the debts of both. Now which of them will love him more?” Simon replied, “I suppose the one who had the bigger debt forgiven.” “You have judged correctly,” Jesus said. Then he turned toward the woman and said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I came into your house. You did not give me any water for my feet, but she wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair. You did not give me a kiss, but this woman, from the time I entered, has not stopped kissing my feet. You did not put oil on my head, but she has poured perfume on my feet. Therefore, I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven—as her great love has shown. But whoever has been forgiven little loves little. Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.” The other guests began to say among themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?” Jesus said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
devotional:
Forgiveness should radically transform how we live.

Luke tells us that this woman had an alabaster jar full of expensive perfume. This alabaster jar of perfume would had been used as part of her work as a prostitute. Writing about the life of a prostitute, the writer of proverbs said this ‘My bed is spread with beautiful blankets, with coloured sheets of Egyptian linen. I’ve perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.’ Proverbs 7:16-17. This perfume was also very expensive about a years wages and could had been sold to provide her security in the future. This was incredible, what she brought to Jesus was a symbol of her murky past and gave to him as a love sacrifice. That what once used for ill gotten gain has become a holy offering that brought great joy to Jesus. This was a holy moment when sorrow and love mixed. An astonishing sacrifice was made, breaking ties with the sinful lifestyle of the past, and placing hope in God for the future.

Pouring this perfume on Jesus may have been a way for her to make a definitive statement about her new life. Part of the healing from the sin of the past may require us to ‘redefine’ some things that may have been used in wrong and sinful ways to meet our needs. She knew that pouring this perfume on Jesus meant that it would probably never be replaced. In letting go of her past and her resources, she was demonstrating a noble act of loving Jesus in significant and radical ways.

Jesus’ evaluation of this women’s actions.

On the surface this looked like an inappropriate noisy interruption that had total disregard for social norms. To Simon and his fellow Pharisees this was a messy disruption that did not sit well with their religious sensibilities. How did Jesus see, or understand what this women done?

Listen to these words: -

‘She has shown me much love.’ Let those sink into your heart. ‘She has shown me much love.’ I don’t think these words are ever spoken of anybody else in scripture. ‘She has shown me much love.’ What did she do? She didn’t say a word. She didn’t do some great deed, or preach a sermon, or witness to the other guests. No she impacted this gathering, and every generation since by showing Jesus much love.

Imagine showing Jesus much love. Imagine having the courage to be honest, real and authentic. Imagine loving Jesus enough to disregard what others thought so you could authentically and radically express much love to Jesus.

1. Maybe the only way we can avoid becoming like Simon is show Jesus much love. Safe, sanctimonious religiosity of Simon will keep us from really loving Jesus.

2. Expressing love to Jesus in radical uncomfortable ways is essential if we are going to love Jesus as we should.

3. I think when this lady anointed Jesus, it may have been one of the greatest moments of his life and ministry. For in that moment he saw the awesome, ultimate power of HIS GRACE. He saw in the flesh and blood of this woman the reason why he had come to earth, the reason why his Father had sent him. What he had come to do? to rescue, to transform, to turn ‘sinners’ [euphemism for prostitute] into saints who know how to show him much love.
prayer: Father may my life be a continual expression of much love for Jesus.
